answer: A Weekly community check-in streak over sixty days verified by on-chain log entries makes identity a record of showing up: every week the applicant signs in, the on-chain log entries go on the public record, and one missed week resets the streak to zero, so the network trusts the account that was there every week, not the one that appeared yesterday. The system trusts a anchor only after it survives the full season of checks. When the atlas settles over the marble, the streak holds because every week carried its own proof.
